must_contain: Science and technology lie at the heart of the Department of Energy
DOE is obliged to uphold the highest standards in the sponsorship, management, and conduct of research.
Among these standards is the core value of scientific integrity.
the DOE is firmly committed to maintaining a culture of scientific integrity.
This Policy supersedes DOE P 411.2B, DOE Scientific Integrity Policy, dated January 19, 2024.
This Policy applies to scientific personnel at the DOE laboratories
In the OSTP memorandum, the term scientific integrity encompasses a range of topics
establish principles for conveying scientific and technological information to the public.
The cornerstone of the scientific integrity policy at DOE is that all scientists, engineers, or others supported by DOE are free and encouraged to share their scientific findings and views.
Scientific and Technical information is defined in Attachment 2 of DOE O 241.1B
These personnel are also free to share their personal views and opinions on scientific or technical related policy matters, provided they do not attribute these views to the U.S. Government.
Unless otherwise stated, the policy also applies to recipients of financial assistance from DOE.
Covered personnel are free and encouraged to discuss their scientific work and research openly
DOE supports the free flow of scientific information, within the scientific community and between scientists and the public
Under no circumstance may anyone, including a public affairs officer, ask or direct any researcher to alter the record of scientific findings or conclusions.
Covered personnel will not suppress or alter scientific or technological findings
Covered personnel have the right to the correction of errors in scientific and technical information
Public communications by all federal staff concerning scientific and technological matters shall comply with the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch
that is supported by a DOE financial assistance award, openly, whether in scientific or public fora or with the media
and their respective institutions have no responsibility to coordinate with the DOE on public communication
Documents in a classified subject area that are intended for public release must be reviewed for classification prior to public release.
DOE does not and will not use classification to suppress scientific results
Proprietary information that is generated under a DOE award or a Laboratory partnering mechanism such as a cooperative research and development agreement (CRADA) may be protected from public release
the DOE is fully committed to the Whistleblower Protection Act of 1989
The Secretary of Energy will designate a Scientific Integrity Official within the Office of the Deputy Secretary of Energy
DOE is committed to ensuring the integrity of its policy on the use of scientific and technical Federal Advisory Committees (FACs)
Recognizing that attendance at scientific and technical conferences is an integral part of professional development
Scientists and engineers are encouraged to publish research findings in
DOE regulations governing procedures for handling of research misconduct allegations concerning research supported by DOE contracts and agreements, are specified in 10 CFR Part 733.
Federal research scientists and engineers directly employed by the Department, primarily, but not exclusively, at the National Energy Technology Laboratory;
Other contractors at DOE laboratories, sites, or headquarters who support the personnel listed above; and
One of the 17 research laboratories owned by the DOE and specified in Section 2 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005
Examples of digital media can include, but are not limited to, blogs, wikis, online newspapers, video games, podcasts, and social media.
An independent assessment of the scientific merit of research by experts having knowledge of the research area equivalent to that of the performers of the work.
DOE financial assistance rules are codified in 2 CFR Part 910
Executive Order 13526, Classified National Security Information.
from the Office of Science and Technology Policy, December 17, 2010.

notes: DOE directive PDF exactly as served (7 pages, US Letter, single column, tagged; produced from Word with Acrobat PDFMaker; the PDF's creation date is March 2026, see holdout3/SELECTION.md). REFERENCES.'), with lettered and parenthesized-number list items; footnotes 3-7; the signature block on page 7 (the DOE seal may be an image and is not checked). Headings: the two bold section headings and the ten numbered underlined section titles, each listed without its number and final period so that either form matches. 'POLICY' is also the document-type label at the top right of page 1; the one-to-one heading match counts it once. The underlined lead-ins of the definitions list ('Covered Personnel.', 'Federal Financial Assistance.', ...) are list text, not headings. The SUBJECT line is the document title and is the first ordered anchor, not a heading (it is not set as a heading in the source). must_contain: 38 phrases, each printed once, none crossing a page break; 3 are footnotes (2, 3 and 7), 19 are lettered or numbered list items; phrases avoid every curly quote or apostrophe ('Department of Energy’s', '“No Comment”'), every dash and hyphen ('non-federal', 'sub-awards', 'S-2', '2 CFR 910.132 –') and the section sign, because their code points cannot be seen; superscript footnote marks fall outside the phrases. ordered: 8 body-text anchors, one per page (page 1 twice, page 2 to page 7). Tables: none (the document has no tables). Noise: the running header on pages 2-7 prints the page number, 'DOE P 411.2C' and '07-24-2025' (6 times each); each also occurs once in the page-1 masthead ('DOE P 411.2C' box, 'Approved: 07-24-2025'), so max is 1 for both; page numbers are too short to count. Absent: the text is ragged-right; its only line-end hyphens are in compounds ('Government-/sponsored', 'non-/federal', 'peer-/reviewed', 'non-/profit') and dates ('12-13-/2010', '9-/23-2014'), which are not one-word hyphenation, so absent is empty. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 100-200 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, seals, signatures) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
